quest.title: Treasure Voyage
quest.description: Miitoboru, a waverider who claims to be a mighty pirate ship, seems to have something to discuss with you...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3

talks.objective: Go talk to Miitoboru

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Ahoy there! You're finally here. I've been waiting for a long time. Even my deck is getting burrs.

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: But this boat... does this boat even have a deck? This is a dinghy at most, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Who would've thought that I, the notorious pirate ship commanded by Ako Domeki would one day end up like this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you're a big pirate ship? But who's Ako Domeki?

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: What? You don't even know who Ako Domeki is?

choices.text: Never heard of them.

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Ako Domeki Zaemon? Defender of Seirai? The name of the most feared pirate ever to sail the seas... *sigh* Who would've thought...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nope, the name doesn't ring a bell... Alright Miitoboru, you told us to come here, so tell us... What is this all about?

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: It feels so weird being called that all of a sudden. Ugh... You see, as I said, I'm here because I drifted here...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: So I'm thinking my original body must be nearby... It feels strange using the word "body," haha... but I do need to find it as soon as possible.

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: I've lost track of how long I've been sleeping here, but I'm certain my companions will still be waiting for me. I need to find my body, get shipshape, and return to them as soon as possible!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Aye, but I can't make it there on my own. After all, a talking ship is just a ship. It still needs someone at the wheel.

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Let's make a deal. You help me find my body, and I will help you find treasure in return!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Treasure!

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: I'm a pirate ship after all! Call it a pirate ship's intuition, or some kind of sixth sense — either way, the moment I woke up, I could sense that this area is filled with valuable treasures.

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: You have my word, a pirate ship always finds its treasure, argh! Or may I be blighted with barnacles! What say ye, me hearties — do we have an accord?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, let's help Miitoboru. If he finds his body and we get treasure in return, everybody wins!

choices.text: He had you at "treasure," huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hee-hee... {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: #So, {NICKNAME}... Will you help me, or not?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'd be delighted.

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Great! Well, there's a place I wanted to go to as soon as I woke up. Based on my pirate ship's intuition, there's be some big treasure hidden there! Argh! Let's head there and search for it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Time to set sail!

choices.text: I had a feeling that might swing it for you.
I... may have heard of them?

talks.objective: Go to the place Miitoboru sensed
Investigate the shipwreck

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this really the right place? There's nothing here but a shipwreck...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Miitoboru had better not be lying to us... Guess it's time to go back and ask our friend a couple of questions, {NICKNAME}!

talks.objective: Talk to Miitoboru

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: How did it go? Did you find anything valuable?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph, Miitoboru!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmph, Miitoboru!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There is nothing on this island except for a shipwreck. What kind of intuition is that?

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: What? No, impossible...

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Ah, I know! It must be because I have been sleeping for too long, and my intuition is not as sharp as it once was. Uhhh, as the saying goes, nobody's perfect, and certainly no boat's perfect either, right? Cut me a little slack, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: The next place will be the one... I'm sure the next place will be full of treasure...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It'd better be! No more playing tricks on us this time!

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: You have my word! ...But, um... the next place is a little far away, and I'm not sure of the precise location. All I know is that... it's somewhere northwest of here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But there are so many islands in the northwest! You gotta give us a little more than that!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a minute... If you mean one of the larger islands, there are only two of them in the northwest.

choices.text: The island full of raven statues...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Hmm... Now that you mention it, I do sense the cawing of ravens coming from over there...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: But not just the sound of ravens, no... there be music as well...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: To be precise, the "cawing" is coming from the east, and the "music" is coming from the southwest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you're hearing two sounds? Ugh... where could this darn treasure be...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But where can you hear the sounds from both islands at the same time...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Somewhere in between the two.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Oh, you're right, {NICKNAME}... Yup! That's exactly what Paimon was thinking too!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Excellent work, Paimon.

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Argh! Then let's go over and take a look! Hahahaha...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: You know... I must say, it seems you two are quite close.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You bet! We've been on loads of adventures together and found lots of treasure before!

choices.text: Paimon is the best companion one could ask for!

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Argh... if only I'd been able to speak back when we were sailing on the sea, then maybe I would've been able to communicate with my companions just like you two...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: You seem to have so much fun together, I'm a little jealous.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hee-hee...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Alright! Time to find the center location of these two big islands!

choices.text: Paimon is the best guide in all of Teyvat!
The island where musical flowers grow...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Musical flowers, hmm? Indeed... among the sounds I'm sensing, I hear music drifting across the sea...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: But not just the sound of music, no... there's the non-stop cawing of ravens, too...

talks.objective: Go to the place Miitoboru sensed
Go to the place Miitoboru sensed
Go to the place Miitoboru sensed

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, surprise, surprise... There's nothing here either, except yet another shipwreck... well, half a shipwreck, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Was there no treasure this whole time? Um... Oh... But wait, both times Miitoboru thought he was sensing treasure, it turned out to be shipwrecks... Does that mean this is his body!?

choices.text: Maybe boats have a special platonic bond that draws them together.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What does that mean? ...Ohhh, like they're ship-friends?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}, why don't we take a picture of the boat and show it to Miitoboru...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then he can confirm whether it's his body or not!

choices.text: It is possible.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Not only did it break into two pieces, but the parts are also completely tattered...

talks.objective: Take a picture of the shipwreck

dialogues.speaker: Start Taking Photos
dialogues.text: Photograph Placeholder

talks.objective: Talk to Miitoboru
Talk to Miitoboru

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Miitoboru!

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: There you are, how did it go? Did you find something? Let me guess, you found a huge—

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: *sigh* A huge load of nothing? Ugh... I dropped the cannonball again, didn't I?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Same as last time. Just another shipwreck.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe they're parts of your body? We took pictures of them, take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Show the picture of the shipwreck...)

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Is this a painting? I didn't know you two could paint so well. Just look at the detail, down to the smallest blade of grass... It's just like the real thing!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We didn't paint this. We took it using a Kamera.

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: So it was drawn by a machine, through some high-speed mechanism...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, even the mighty pirate ship has never seen a Kamera before!

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: What are you trying to say? It's not like I haven't seen similar things before. It's just like the Hell Paintings in all those legends.

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: But anyway, what's that thing in the middle of this... picture?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's the shipwreck we found... Take a look! Could it be... your body?

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Ha, impossible! Where did this sorry ship come from? It's a total wreck.

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: You may not know this, but I'm considered as the mightiest pirate ship of the Ako Domeki fleet. My hull is made of the best wood found on Seirai Island.

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: The edges of my frame boards were refined with folding saws so that the pieces fit together perfectly. Then they were joined together and reinforced with large rivets, making me indestructible... There's no way I could end up like this!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But your intuition led us to shipwrecks twice in a row...

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: It's probably because of the special bond between all boats that draws us to one another. Before they ran aground, these ships may well have been self-aware too. The remnants of their spirit is most likely what I sensed.

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Anyway, this can't be my body... My body is probably docked at a hidden port somewhere in these waters.

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: You'll see... My side panels are painted with the finest lacquer. Argh, what a majestic sight I used to be.

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Once we find it, you'll realize how different I am from this shipwreck in your picture.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That sounds great! We should go for a cruise together sometime.

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Argh, that's for sure!

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: I can't believe I sensed the wrong thing twice in a row... The lack of maintenance has really taken the wind out of my sails as far as my intuition goes.

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: You have to apply caulk once in a while if you want a long-lasting voyage. That goes for people, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What the heck is "caulk"? Is it the glue that holds all the parts of the ship together?

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Haha, Paimon, you're a funny one, aren't you. No, but you're not that far off!

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Caulk is the stuff we use to fill the gaps between the planks to stop water from leaking into the ship. It's made of rubber or something. Every once in a while, you gotta caulk the gaps as part of the maintenance!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just like how people need a good rest once in a while.

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Exactly. Which reminds me, I got some good rest when you two went on that little adventure, I'm sure I'll be able to sense where the real treasure is now!

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Third time's the charm! Time to get serious. We'll definitely find something this time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon sure hopes so... Anything will do at this point...

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: What's wrong, Paimon? You don't sound like you believe me...

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Anyway... This time, I sense something in the southeast, on the sea surface. It doesn't feel like something very big. And that raises the chances of it being a small but valuable item, hahaha.

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Come on, let's go!

talks.objective: Go to the place Miitoboru sensed
Investigate the reef on the sea surface
Investigate the reef on the sea surface

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Surely you found something this time!

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Have I finally convinced you of this mighty pirate ship's razor-sharp treasure-hunting senses!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All there was was a bird's nest...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So yeah, technically there were a couple of eggs... but that was all.

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Oh... just, uh, just the two, you say?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? So this is the valuable treasure you were talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Ahem, Paimon, you may not be aware, but the mightier the pirate ship, the longer its voyage at sea, you see... Eventually, the only food available onboard is dry fish...

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: At times like this, a couple of bird eggs on a reef nearby can easily become the most valuable treasure to a crew.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Miitoboru...

choices.text: Your excuses are so lame...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Okay, fine... But how the heck did I end up sensing eggs? How strange...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: I swear I sensed something!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But there's nothing else on the reef...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Could it be these two planks? Seems like they were used as a shelter. Paimon wonders where they came from...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait, this plank...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What happened? What was that?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Was that someone's memory?

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: *sigh*...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: #I know where this plank comes from. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, what you saw just now was my own memory.

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: It was my first time sailing on the sea after I was built. The crew used greased planks to create a slipway, then launched me into the water...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: The thing is, it's really hard to control the angle at which the bow launches onto the water. It could very well break if you're not careful, which is why most people choose to launch the ship sideways instead.

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: These two planks... Or should I say, these two side panels... They must have been the first parts of my body to make contact with the water.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Miitoboru... If your side panels are here, does that mean...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: ...Maybe I crashed into the reef here and was shattered to pieces long ago... And maybe the sensation I had when I woke up wasn't some kind of treasure-hunting intuition after all, but me responding to my own body...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: There I was, making fun of that shipwreck, blissfully unaware that I was actually making fun of my own body. Haha... Ah, how embarrassing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We don't know that for sure! Maybe... maybe your body is still in one piece! Yeah, these two planks are probably just, um... part of your... family tree!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You mean they're... wood-relatives?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, could share the same roots! Even it's if not, there are loads of shipwrecks around here. These planks probably just belong to one of them.

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: But...

choices.text: Paimon is right.

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: I... *sigh* Thank you, both of you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By the way, Miitoboru, wasn't there something about your name mentioned in that memory? Do you remember your name now?

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: ...It's a pity, but I'm afraid I didn't see much more than you did. I still can't recall my name...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that's a shame...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: #It's not too bad! You and {NICKNAME} can keep calling me Miitoboru. It's a good name!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hee-hee, of course it is, Paimon picked it, after all. So, Miitoboru, is there anywhere else you want to go?

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Although I can sense two more places... I fear it will be the same situation as before. No treasures, only some driftwood...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It doesn't matter!

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Argh... but I swore there'd be treasure in this deal for you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, it's okay, Miitoboru... we're friends now!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Friends don't do deals.

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Well, in that case... Whether it's treasure or not, let's hope you two can find something rather than nothing there.

choices.text: It's fine either way.

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Haha, good! Let's go to the closer location first!

choices.text: Whatever the booty, we'll take it!
There are other possibilities.
That's nonsense.

talks.objective: Go to the place Miitoboru sensed
Look for pieces of Miitoboru on nearby beaches
Look for pieces of Miitoboru on nearby beaches

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure enough, no treasure here...

choices.text: Does that really matter?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knows that! ...Paimon just can't help feeling a little disappointed, that's all...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's a wooden sword here. It looks like a children's toy...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Then it's perfect for Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey!

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: The thing I sensed... Could it be this wooden sword?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Surely it couldn't be a wooden sword...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I think it actually might be the wooden sword...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, that lightning was really powerful! What's this memory about?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can still feel her head spinning...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Shiver me timbers!!! I remember now. The sea battle between Ako Domeki and the Shogunate. And then the lightning that came at the end of the battle...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: *sigh*... What could it have been?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon has no idea. It was really scary, though.

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Wait... So that thunderstorm was the reason I... the reason I drifted here. Aye, I was terribly injured in that storm. My whole body was falling apart...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: It took all my strength to get here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, Miitoboru... But what about the wooden sword? What does this have to do with it?

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Zaemon once seized a sword-wielding Maguu with his barbed spear. The Maguu drifted here with us. The wooden sword was probably crafted by local children, imitating the Maguu's sword...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: The body of the mighty pirate ship that once fought against the Shogunate, now reduced to a children's toy, of all things... Argh... my mind is awash with strange and complex feelings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So Miitoboru, should we take this with us? After all... it is a part of you...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: ...No, there's no point taking this now. Hmph, young scallywags... the little landlubbers got me this time!

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: ...*sigh* Although it's disappointing now that I remember the truth, somehow I feel relieved, too... At least I know what happened. I won't be deceiving myself with my wishful thinking any longer.

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: The only thing I'm worried about now is my old mateys who drifted here with me... I wish I could know how they're doing.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm sure they'll be fine.

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Aye, let's hope so... Okay, there's one last place...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: I can feel it... it's the last piece of my body.

choices.text: Treasure isn't the be-all and end-all...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's left of the Thunderbird's wrath...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Well blow me down... Just a fraction of the Thunderbird's wrath, and yet still so powerful...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: #Wait! But the lightning came from Seirai Island... {NICKNAME}, have you ever been there? Do you know what happened to the island after that?

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: No... I can't believe it... It was a truly terrible thunderstorm, it was... ah, I don't have the words to describe the horror of it.

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: We stood up against the Shogunate precisely because we did not want our homeland to be ruled by them. We wanted to protect the people of Seirai Island...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: We made an enemy of the Shogunate for the sake of Seirai Island, and in the end... Oh, Shrine Maiden... Why...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Wait... So that thunderstorm was the reason I... the reason I drifted here. Aye, I was terribly injured in that storm. My whole body was falling apart...

response.speaker: Miitoboru

response.text: This wooden sword... is made from my broken timber...

dialogues.text: There are a lot of wooden planks on this conch house... But they don't look like what we're after...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Could it be the one on the stone?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it, though? A board nailed onto two wooden strips, with a wooden mallet next to it...

choices.text: This is a musical instrument...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This? Is a musical instrument? Can it really make a decent sound?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, why don't we try it out first before giving it to Miitoboru?

response.speaker: The Wooden Instrument
response.text: (The intact wood strips made a cool and crisp sound, while the damaged wood strips only made a muffled, heavy sound like ordinary wood...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's pretty sure this instrument hasn't been repaired in a looong time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, {NICKNAME}, this must be the last fragment of Miitoboru's body. Come on, let's go tell him!

choices.text: I think you hit the wooden strips with the mallet...

talks.objective: Look for pieces of Miitoboru
Talk to Miitoboru

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: You're back. How did it go? Did you find anything?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Show the wooden musical instrument...)

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: This is indeed my last piece... But what the festering fishbait have they turned me into this time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We think it's a musical instrument! But it hasn't been fixed for a while, so you can't really play anything with it...

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: It that so? Argh, a pity, to be sure. Musical instrument... Hehe, I never imagine that my broken body could be used to play music...

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: It makes me think of my old mates... They used to sing when the mood took them...

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: #They'd sit by the beach, facing the campfire... Hey, what kind of sound does this instrument make? Why don't you give it a try. {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... it hasn't been caulked for a long time, so it might not sound as good as you're hoping.

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: #It doesn't matter. Satisfy my curiosity! Just strike it and see what happens, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Strike the intact part of the musical instrument...)

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Argh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So they found a way back...

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Aye... But since I was so badly damaged, it was the most I could do to bring them here. There was no way I could go back with them.

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Ah... It gladdens my heart to know that they are safe, but I... Even though I said goodbye to them, I still can't help thinking, what if I could have gone back with them...

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Oh, how I wish we had returned together. With them, I would have been willing to go anywhere, no matter how dangerous...

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: There are so many grand adventures for us to go on, so many treasures out there in the world, waiting for us to discover them.

dialogues.speaker: Miitoboru
dialogues.text: Why did I have to be left here, abandoned like this? I could do nothing but watch them leave and embark on a new journey... without me.

choices.text: That's how partings go, I guess...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Aye... I still feel the sadness now that I remember it, even after all this time.

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Anyway, thank you for helping me remember all of this, thank you kindly. I'm afraid, though, that they seem to have taken most of the treasure with them when they left...

choices.text: It doesn't matter.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! In a way, all the things you sensed really were invaluable treasures — to you, at least!

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Aye, it's true. Tis a shame I can't repay your kindness... As a ship, there's only so much I can do...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: But, um... In the future, if I ever need your help again...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #We'll be here for you whenever you need us, Miitoboru! Right, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Of course!

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Fantastic, thank you both! And if you ever voyage in these seas again, I will be your trusty companion!

choices.text: Finding your memory is the most important thing.
But they said goodbye to you with a smile...

response.speaker: Miitoboru
response.text: Laugh when you feel like crying, and press on when you feel like giving up. That's how you survive out on the ocean.
